findings.claim: Pi can permanently lose a notice before any model boundary sees it when its pending buffer evicts the notice or the extension reloads.
findings.evidence: onLine accepts notice records into the same pending map as ordinary mail (lines 196-211), and trim deletes the worst pending record without distinguishing notices (126-133), relying on replayDebt and watch replacement for recovery. For example, with 256 retained p0 records, a newly arriving p0 notice sorts last and is immediately discarded. But the called canonical watch presentation path settles carried notices while constructing the page (src/store/invitation_content.rs:2755-2762); settle_offered_notices advances digest_notice_offer (src/store/attention.rs:1333-1348), and a notice whose ordinal is not above the frontier is no longer pending (attention.rs:1076-1081). Restarting watch therefore cannot recover that notice. Reload has the same loss even without saturation: close preserves only proposals in RECOVERY (extension line 293), while the new owner initializes pending to an empty Map (line 327), discarding any watched notice not yet proposed. This does not challenge the intentional watch presentation confirmation contract; the new client incorrectly treats already-carried notices as replayable durable mail. README promises displaced/omitted bodies remain pending and canonical replay recovers them, which is false for these notices. No tests were executed; evidence is the frozen source at 62bc385d0b3623243db43c2536658eec6451f9bd.

findings.claim: A missing Pi mode witness silently disables all enrollment and delivery instead of reporting the required local capability diagnostic.
findings.evidence: The session_start handler returns immediately on ctx.mode !== "tui", including undefined, before creating an owner or calling diagnostic. Every later callback requires callbackOwner(ctx), so this session remains entirely disconnected with no integration warning. This differs from intentionally excluding explicit rpc/json/print modes: design.md D1 explicitly requires "Missing mode or required APIs disables the integration capability with a local diagnostic" so runtime API incompatibility is visible. The adjacent missing-sessionManager check does emit "boundary API unavailable", but the missing-mode case never reaches it. extension.test.mjs:423-425 explicitly exercises mode undefined and checks only that no calls occur, leaving the required diagnostic untested. No external Pi behavior is assumed: the finding is the implemented missing-witness failure path.

findings.claim: The transformed-boundary negative qualification can pass without the target frame ever reaching the transformer because it releases the held turn before observing channel delivery or an exact transformed proposal.
findings.evidence: Proved missing prerequisite, not a reproduced failure. case_negative intends to prove that a returned full-frame proposal rejected before persistence cannot settle a receipt (lines 594-596). It awaits send CLI completion at line 602, touches transform and release-text immediately, waits only for agent_settled, then asserts pending (603-606). The fixture transformer in scripts/pi_tui_fixtures/provider.mjs transforms only entries already present in its turn_end event; the production extension proposals are built from asynchronously received watch rows in integrations/pi/extension/herdr-threads.js. CLI send completion does not establish receipt by that child watch. A feasible interleaving delays watch delivery until after both turn_end and agent_before_settle: neither boundary proposes the target, the run settles, and pending passes trivially. Delivery can then arrive before the explicit retry at 608, producing the expected acknowledgment at 609, so the complete case passes without exercising rejection. Unlike cancel_settle_probe, which checks the exact message ID and body in settle_abort.entries, this case never verifies that its target appeared at the transformed boundary. Preserve the pending/recovery assertions and gate release on recipient delivery readiness or assert an observer record containing the exact target proposal and its transformation.

findings.claim: The native IO test leaves its interval-running watch child alive when the connected-status assertion fails, hanging the Node test process instead of completing failure cleanup.
findings.evidence: Source risk, not reproduced: the README runs this file directly with node --test. The test creates watcher with a Node program that prints one status then runs setInterval indefinitely; it executes assert.equal((await line).state, connected) before await watcher.stop(). Its finally block only removes the scratch directory. If transport decoding regresses so the first delivered row has a different state, that assertion throws and skips stop; nodeIO child() retains referenced child-process/stdout handles and has no parent/test failure cleanup or watch deadline. The same owner therefore keeps the test worker alive after its failed assertion, retaining the child and preventing completion. Move watcher.stop() into guaranteed teardown; also bound the line wait so a missing delivery fails and reaches teardown.

response.evidence: Static end-to-end demonstration against captured head 62bc385: design D4 requires keeping bodies until a qualified boundary, discarding excess bodies without settlement, and canonical replay after capacity release; integrations/pi/README.md Delivery and wake explicitly promises displaced/omitted bodies remain pending. Start with 256 retained small p0 records with no deadlines before a model boundary. extension/herdr-threads.js:196-211 accepts a new notice, defaults its priority to 0, assigns Infinity deadline and the newest sequence. compare and trim (34,126-133) therefore remove this notice as the worst tie and set replayDebt. No proposal or context callback has seen it. In the existing canonical presentation path, invitation_content.rs:2755-2762 settles the carried notice; attention.rs:1333-1348 advances the binding notice frontier, and informational_notice_pending_for at 1076-1081 excludes ordinals at or below it. Crucially, replay is not rescued by a retained presentation outbox: cli/watch.rs:735-755 flushes the JSON line and immediately sends DeliveryPresentationConfirmV2 independently of extension/model acceptance; invitation_content.rs:975-988 retires non-control descriptors, and retire_outbox at 853-884 clears their stored body. Let this normal confirmation finish before capacity release. released/replaceWatch then reconnect (extension lines 148-160), but neither canonical pending notice selection nor the retired outbox supplies the discarded notice. Static failure-path demonstration, not an executed reproduction. The new native IO test (integrations/pi/extension/tests/extension.test.mjs:356-370 at 62bc385) spawns a child with an indefinite setInterval, awaits the first line, asserts its state, and only then calls watcher.stop(). A failed state assertion therefore skips the only stop; finally removes only the directory. A missing line also waits indefinitely without reaching finally. nodeIO in herdr-threads.js:396-452 creates a referenced ChildProcess with piped stdout, has no spawn deadline or test-failure cleanup, and only kills it through stop (or an oversized-output condition, which this one-line child does not trigger). The README qualification command runs this file with plain node --test. External runtime premises verified by fetching https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html#subprocessunref (quote: "use the subprocess.unref() method") and https://nodejs.org/api/test.html (forceExit quote: "Default: false."): child references keep the event loop alive, and test completion does not force exit by default. Thus a regression caught by this assertion leaves the interval child alive and the worker awaiting its referenced handles instead of completing qualification. This violates design D8 required owned process/temp cleanup and AGENTS.md:13 requiring test/helper processes to stop before task completion. The test and transport are new in the captured diff.
